claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The proposed intervention is a uniform, approximately 2 μm Al2O3 coating deposited by PVD on the cast alloy.
The deposited alumina layer will remain continuous and adherent on HfNbTaTiZr.
Al2O3 forms a dense and thermally stable oxygen barrier at 1000 °C.
The Al2O3 coating will limit oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Limiting oxygen diffusion will mitigate internal oxidation of HfNbTaTiZr.
Mitigating internal oxidation will preserve the underlying microstructure responsible for the alloy's ductility and yield strength.
After 100 hours in air at 1000 °C, coated samples will have lower oxygen uptake than uncoated samples.
After 100 hours in air at 1000 °C, coated samples will develop thinner oxide scales or avoid deep oxygen penetration relative to uncoated samples.
After high-temperature exposure, coated samples will retain yield strength similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
After high-temperature exposure, coated samples will retain ductility similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant oxidation under the specified 1000 °C, 100-hour air exposure.
Oxidation of uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr under the specified exposure degrades its mechanical performance.
The protective effect will hold at 1000 °C for 100 hours in air during subsequent tensile testing at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Higher temperatures, longer exposures, or loading beyond the stated boundaries may cause coating failure or mechanical-property degradation.
